payload.statement:
# Problem: Council review of Chapter 6, Core Resolution Mechanics (quarto-book/chapters/06-core-resolution.qmd)

You are the hol-rulebook council. Audit this chapter as a publishable unit of the Heroes of Legend
TTRPG rulebook and produce a disposition plan. Do NOT fix anything; file findings only.

## Scope
The registered source `06-core-resolution` (the chapter's .qmd, native Typst). Cross-check against the
rest of the book wherever a claim is canon-determined: character-creation examples and the Kael/Lyra/
Roric/Makeva templates (ch02), skill rank bonuses and the skill roster (ch07), the damage budget and
Basic-card damage floor (ch08 @sec-damage-budget), conditions vocabulary (ch13), armor/DR canon (ch16),
monster damage bands per Challenge (ch20), glossary/term definitions (ch21), reference sheets (ch22).
The chapter covers: the core roll (3d6 + attribute + skill + difficulty), the success-tier table
(Weak 1-8 / Standard 9-14 / Strong 15-18+), totals of zero or less, Boons and Banes (4d6 keep three
highest / lowest), opposed rolls, attack rolls and the always-hit principle, DR, the players-roll-all
convention, Defense Rolls (formula, reading the result, worked examples), Critical Hits (three natural
6s + d6 table), Fumbles (three natural 1s + d6 table), Difficulty Modifiers, and four Worked Examples.

## Locked conventions the chapter must satisfy (cite the violated convention in every finding)
- **Damage budget = FLAT numbers, on the table, no dice.** Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21
  (Weak/Standard/Strong). Basic-card floor is 1/2/3 + attribute modifier. Every damage/healing number in
  this chapter (examples, crit table, fumble table) must be on a budget row, an explicit Basic-card floor,
  or a damage-TIER bump ("+1 damage tier"). "The table is the law."
- **ZERO flat +N damage riders** anywhere in the book (weapons rework 2026-08-19). The canonical way to
  raise damage is "+1 damage tier".
- **One-roll principle (locked):** the attack/hit roll IS the damage roll; no separate roll. The only
  sanctioned dice in the book are 3d6 rolls, 4d6 boon/bane keep-three, and explicit d6/1d4 RANDOM TABLES
  (the Critical Effect d6 table at ch06:155 and the Fumble Complication d6 table at ch06:183 are exactly
  that: sanctioned random tables, NOT damage rolls). Flag any other dice.
- **DR canon (ch16):** DR subtracts from incoming damage; minimum 1 damage from any hit; armor and shields
  grant DR and never add to the Defense Roll. Verify every DR number used in the chapter's examples against
  the ch16 armor table and against the ch20 stat blocks it names (goblin, Knight of the Iron Circle).
- **Monster damage bands (ch20, locked):** C1-2 = 2/4/6, C3-6 = 6/9/12, C7+ = 9/15/21; a secondary attack
  is at most one tier lower. Any monster damage value quoted in this chapter's examples must match the
  stat block in ch20 AND sit on its challenge band.
- **Condition vocabulary (ch13):** leveled conditions use "Name X" (Burning X, Slowed X, Frightened X...),
  binary conditions by name (Prone, Stunned, Restrained). Bespoke near-conditions and retired vocabulary
  are findings.
- **Cross-references:** every @sec-* link must resolve to a real label; every chapter/section named in
  prose must exist; cross-chapter claims (skill bonuses, weapon/item names, conditions) must match canon.
- **Style law: ZERO em-dashes** in prose (added lines included). No "Standard+" style undefined degrees.
- **Native-Typst migration conventions (MIGRATION-SPEC, binding):** exactly ONE `{=typst}` fence per file
  with the `# H1` line kept above it; callout bodies in the NAMED `body: [...]` form (positional is
  silently dropped); every `#table(` carrying `outlined: false`; `#label("sec-...")` on the line after its
  heading.

## Known defect class in this chapter (verify, quantify, and rule on disposition)
The markdown-to-Typst migration had two list-rendering regressions, both observable in the built PDF
(quarto-book/_output/Heroes-of-Legend.pdf) and both mechanical to fix:
1. **Collapsed enum.** ch06:91 `#enum(numbering: "1.")[ ... ]` holds three hard-wrapped formula lines in
   one `[ ]` body. Typst joins newlines inside `[...]` into a single paragraph, so the PDF renders ONE
   run-on item: "1. No defensive skill: 3d6 + Agility modifier - Challenge Dodge: 3d6 + Agility modifier +
   Dodge rank - Challenge Parry: 3d6 + Brawn modifier + Parry rank - Challenge". The three formulas must be
   three list items. Five other chapters carry the same `#enum(numbering: "1.")[` multi-line shape
   (01-introduction:108, 02-character-creation:26, 19-gm-guidance:339, 20-bestiary:667,
   22-reference-sheets:239) and need the same check.
2. **Bullets became numbers.** ch06:97-101 were a markdown BULLET list (`- **Agility** ...`) and are now a
   Typst `+ ` enumeration, so the PDF numbers them 1..5. The same `+ `-for-bullet substitution is
   book-wide (197 `+ ` items across 11 chapters; the pre-migration sources used `- `).
Rule on scope: is each of these a ch06-local fix or a book-wide sweep? The orchestrator will implement
whatever the council recommends; say explicitly which.

## Findings format (one finding per member this round)
Each finding must be decision-oriented: name the broken value with [06-core-resolution:LINE], the
expected/correct value, the violated convention, and the minimal fix. Cite cross-chapter canon lines where
the expected value is canon-determined. Severity is implicit in the fix size. Do NOT invent defects to
look thorough; a chapter with few real problems is a good outcome.

payload.argument: Chapter 6's load-bearing numbers do not survive recomputation, so the chapter must change. Headline: the Knight of the Iron Circle is credited a Strong damage of 5 [06-core-resolution:144], but the same Challenge 3 adversary carries the longsword triple 6/9/12 in the bestiary [20-bestiary:133] and is resolved with a Standard of 9 in the combat chapter [13-combat:468], so Strong must be 12; against Kael's leather DR 2 that is 10 damage, not the printed 3, and the plate branch at :146 leaves 6, not the asserted floor of 1. Two clauses contradict themselves: the defense example at :140 prints a 4+3+5 dice sum as 13 when the faces give 12 (the net +1 is folded away), and the Roric passage at :240 reduces the greataxe hit to 2 and then describes that same swing as five. Makeva's lock at :242 is rolled with Sleight of Hand, but the skill roster assigns opening locks to Thievery [07-skills:207] and runs the same character's strongbox scene with Thievery [07-skills:99,101]. The Critical table's face 1 doubles the tier instead of taking the canonical single step [09-talents-abilities:108], landing Adept and Master crits at 24 and 42, past the budget ceiling of 21. Two migration regressions are observable in the built PDF: the defense formulas merge into one numbered line and the five defense bullets print as numbers [full.txt:7455-7457]. Scope: the damage, skill-key, arithmetic, and critical fixes are chapter-local; the list-rendering regressions and the one-low chapter number on the armor link originate in the book-wide Typst migration, yet Chapter 6 still needs its own correction. Support side: Kael's attack chain reconciles (12 + 1 = 13 Standard; 2 + 1 = 3; DR 2 leaves 1), the goblin's 2/4/6 and the troll's DR 3 match the bestiary, all four cross-references resolve, both d6 tables use every face once, and the fumble self-damage and critical healing values sit on budget rows.

evidence.claim: Recomputation against canon: 2+3+2=7 dice, minus the net penalty 1, gives 6, a Weak defense; the adversary's real Strong value 12 is then reduced by leather DR 2 to 10, or by plate DR 6 to 6, never 3 and never the floor of 1.
The Knight example states a Strong damage of 5 and a post-armor result of 3; the canon Strong value for that adversary is 12, so the resulting damage should be 10.
The bestiary fixes the Challenge 3 Knight's only weapon as a longsword on the 6/9/12 triple, placing Strong at 12 on the locked C3-6 band.
The combat chapter resolves the identical Challenge 3 defense and states the adversary's Standard damage as 9, which confirms the triple and therefore a Strong of 12.
The plate branch inherits the wrong 5 and claims the floor of 1; with the corrected 12 and DR 6 the outcome is 6 damage.
The goblin defense example reports a 4+3+5 roll as 13; the faces sum to 12 and only the net +1 yields 13, so the modifier step is folded into the dice total.
The goblin's scimitar triple is 2/4/6 on the C1-2 band, so the Standard 4 used in the example is canon-correct.
The greataxe example subtracts troll DR 3 from 5 to reach 2, then re-describes that same swing as five; the post-reduction number is 2.

payload.argument: Refute: at least one printed number is off the damage budget and two fumble entries are undefined mechanics. (1) The Critical table's top result doubles an attack's Strong value. A Master attack doubles 21 to 42, and even an Adept card doubles 12 to 24, which is above the budget's highest row. Neither value sits on a row, on the Basic floor (1/2/3 plus attribute), or on a sanctioned tier bump. The book already prices critical damage as a single-row increase with a 21 ceiling (Death Blow, ch09), so the expected fix is to replace the doubling with '+1 damage tier, one row up, maximum 21'. (2) The Knight of the Iron Circle's Strong damage prints as 5 (ch06:144, ch06:146); the Challenge-3 Knight in ch20 carries a longsword at 6/9/12, so the expected Strong value is 12, and the follow-on result (12 minus leather DR 2 = 10, not the printed 3) is wrong too. (3) The friendly-fire fumble hands an ally a Weak amount without naming which card or row supplies it, and it can fire on a tripled 1 from a non-attack roll where no weapon swing exists; the minimal fix is to name the source (the triggering attack's weapon Weak value) or a fixed row. (4) 'Armor degrades one step' presupposes a degradation ladder that exists nowhere; ch16's armor table is flat DR only. (5) The chapter calls tripled 1s automatic failures while also promising every attack connects, so it is undefined whether a fumbled attack still deals its Weak damage. Second Wind's 6 HP is legal: it is on the Novice Strong / Adept Weak row, and ch04's renamed Human gift heals the same 6. 'Blinding Strike' appears neither in this chapter nor anywhere in the book, so there is no value to audit. Tier bands, the min-1-damage clause, boon/bane (4d6 keep three) and DR subtraction all match canon. Migration: the ch06:91 collapsed enum merges the three Defense Roll formulas into one item in the built PDF. That is presentation plus a formula-list obscuring, not a value change, so it is a chapter-local content fix, but the same enum shape recurs in five other chapters and needs a sweep; the ch06:97-101 bullet-to-number swap is cosmetic and book-wide.

The bare-line enum at 22-reference-sheets:239 fails identically (p361), while the four enums that do carry '+' markers (01-introduction:108 p23, 02-character-creation:26 p36, 19-gm-guidance:339 p307, 20-bestiary:667 p338) dodge the collapse but still mis-number as one outer entry containing lettered a/b/c sub-items. The former hyphen bullets at ch06:97-101 now print 1-5 (p123-124), and the same '+'-for-hyphen substitution runs through the book: 197 top-level '+' lines in 11 chapter files, with pre-migration ch13 and ch15 using hyphens and the PDF printing numbers at p203 and p234. Two narrower items: the doubled period is book-wide (20 instances, ch06's is 'Chapter 17..' on p124) and comes from chapter cross-references carrying their own trailing period, so fix the reference format or all 20 sites, not just this chapter; the minus-sign loss is genuinely ch06-only (pre-migration file had 7 U+2212, current file has none, while 08-disciplines, 13-combat and 21-glossary still carry U+2212), so restore those in the ch06 pass. Table captions are a pending book-wide convention decision (only 9 of 138 tables carry a numbered caption prefix), so do not edit ch06's captions in isolation. payload.argument: Chapter 6 fails its own voice-and-consistency bar, though the character work and the absence of draft residue are genuinely clean. (1) Over-saturation: the always-hit / one-roll claim is asserted four separate times inside the chapter (the opener teaser at :23, the Attack Rolls lead at :65, the damage-budget note at :73, and a callout at :77-79), and the defense-reversal idea is restated three times back to back (:122, :124, :132). (2) Stock-phrase reuse: Table 6.1 recycles the introduction chapter's tier copy, including the same closing image the intro already used at 01:94. (3) Rationale stacking: the chapter carries three separate design-rationale blocks (:43-47, :77-79, :126-132) where sibling ch13 instead cross-references ch06 for rationale; at least two should be cut or folded. (4) Term collision: 'Challenge' carries three senses with no disambiguation and no glossary entry for the penalty sense (:101 introduces it as a DA penalty, ch13 calls it a rating, ch20/ch21 define it as monster difficulty), and the chapter's own Difficulty Modifiers table (:205-226) shares the same -6..+4 range, so a reader cannot tell a Challenge from a Difficulty Modifier. The sign convention also flips between chapters (ch06 writes the penalty with a leading minus, ch16 writes the bare rating that is then subtracted), and ch06's goblin value contradicts the bestiary's challenge band; I leave the numeric reconciliation to the mechanics lens and flag only the naming/notation collision here. (5) Flavor balance: only one of the three callouts carries a rule consequence; the other two are pure design rationale, and the worked-example italics ('That's concerning.', 'The chieftain roars, he felt that one.') are decoration with no mechanical job. Character voice itself holds: Kael (Blade), Lyra (Odd), Roric (Protector) and Makeva keep their established class and stat fingerprints from ch01, ch02, ch03 and ch16, with one blemish, that the chapter renames the established Makeva Quickfoot using Lyra's class epithet. No prose draft residue (no TODO/TBD/'we might'/'in a future version'); the only placeholder is the book-wide art caption. Minimal edits recommended: cut the :77-79 rationale callout, fold :122-124 into :105-120, drop the :132 restatement, and add a one-line disambiguation of Challenge at :101 that links the glossary and separates it from a Difficulty Modifier.

payload.argument: The chapter is not yet publishable as a unit; concrete structural and completeness work is required. Cross-references: the chapter's sole explicit reference (line 100) lands in the built PDF as a doubled period and a chapter number one low (the contents page and the chapter opener both number Armor & Shields as Chapter 18 while the reference cites 17); the same defect recurs wherever chapter references resolve (Equipment, Disciplines), so the repair is book-wide, not a ch06-only edit. Duplication: the Combat chapter explicitly points readers here for the full rule, then re-lists the same three defense formulas, the same reversed outcome table, and the same worked defense examples, creating drift risk; this chapter is the correct canonical home and Combat's restatement is the duplication to remove. Placement is otherwise sound: Difficulty Modifiers belong in this chapter, and the GM chapter only comments on applying them without reproducing the ladder, so no duplication exists there. Completeness: the worked-example set exercises the attack roll and skill checks but never an opposed roll or a Boon/Bane, and the Critical and Fumble sections are written only for the attacking roller, leaving three-6s or three-1s on a Defense Roll unstated even though the social-conflict chapter sources the general rule to this chapter; minimum additions are one opposed-roll example, one Boon/Bane example, and a sentence covering Critical/Fumble on a Defense Roll. Conventions: the three unnumbered tables are a partial book-wide convention (chapters 2 and 13 also mix numbered and unnumbered), so a ch06-only edit is not warranted; the collapsed defense enum at line 91 has the same multi-line shape in five other chapters and the bullet-as-number substitution is book-wide, so both need a scope ruling rather than a chapter patch.

payload.argument: The implied support position is that Chapter 6's exception mechanics are internally consistent and stay inside the locked damage budget. Concrete counter-examples break that. A Critical whose d6 bonus is Maximum Damage doubles the Strong value instead of shifting one tier, so a Master-tier attack whose budget Strong is 21 lands for 42, double a ceiling the book states elsewhere and in conflict with the chapters that define a Critical as a flat maximum-Strong 21. The Fumble section calls a fumble an automatic failure while the attack section promises every swing connects and the success table maps totals of 1 through 8 to Weak damage; a three-1 roll totals 3, so the chapter's own arithmetic prescribes Weak damage where the fumble prose prescribes failure, and nothing states which controls on an attack. The Off Balance fumble hands a Boon to the next attack against the hero, but the attacker is an NPC who never rolls; if that Boon is routed to the player's reversed Defense Roll it improves the defender, the opposite of the penalty intended. Gear Damage tells the reader armor loses one step even though the armor chapter models DR as a flat subtraction with no step ladder and the book publishes no repair or degradation rule. And the Defense Roll trigger names only an NPC or monster attacker, leaving hero-versus-hero and NPC-versus-NPC attacks with no defined resolution. Each is closable only by adding explicit caps, ownership of the quoted values, and a stated interaction rule.

payload.argument:
PUBLISHABILITY. Chapter 6 is not publishable as a unit today, but the hold is short: the defect profile is mostly cosmetic sitting on a small load-bearing core. Structure and coverage hold up on independent re-scan (one raw Typst fence with the H1 kept above it, callout bodies in the named form, labels on the line after their headings, every table marked outlined:false, clean H2/H3 hierarchy with no skipped level, no split tables, no orphaned headings, no draft residue, and zero em-dash characters in the source). What blocks release is mechanical, not editorial. Three load-bearing defects: (1) the Knight-of-the-Iron-Circle worked example prints a Strong value that contradicts the Challenge-3 stat block, and both post-armor outcomes inherit the wrong number; (2) the Critical table's top face doubles the Strong value, landing totals on no budget row and above the book's 21 ceiling, which breaches the locked flat-damage convention; (3) three Fumble entries are undefined (friendly fire names no damage source, Off Balance routes a Boon to an NPC who never rolls, Gear Damage assumes a degradation ladder that does not exist), and the fumble-as-automatic-failure line collides with the always-connect guarantee. Those teach or permit non-canon numbers and undefined outcomes, so they gate. Everything else (merged formula list, bullets printing as numbers, doubled reference periods, one-low chapter number, lost minus glyphs, a mis-keyed skill, a renamed hero, prose density) is cosmetic and cheap. Verdict: hold, then release on one TIER 2 pass plus two mechanical sweeps; the Critical and Challenge-vocabulary decisions ship with them or immediately after.

TIER 1, mechanical same-day micro-PR, no mechanics change. (a) ch06:91: the three Defense Roll formulas must render as three separate list items instead of one bracket body; part of a six-file enum sweep. (b) ch06:97-101: the five defense definition lines must be bullets, not numbered items; part of a book-wide marker sweep. (c) ch06:140: the goblin defense line reports a 4+3+5 roll as 13; the faces give 12 and the net +1 supplies the 13, so restore the intermediate step. (d) ch06:240: the greataxe sentence says the hit is reduced to 2 and then re-describes it as five; the post-DR figure is 2 (5 less troll DR 3), so strike or correct the trailing clause. (e) ch06:242: the lock example spends Sleight of Hand where the roster keys lock work to Thievery; swap the skill name, the +1 rank is unchanged because she owns Thievery too. (f) ch06:242: 'Makeva the Odd' drops the established surname; restore Makeva Quickfoot. (g) ch06:100: the armor cross-reference renders with two periods and a one-low chapter number (Armor & Shields is chapter 18, cited as 17); fix the reference format book-wide. (h) ch06:92-94: restore the Unicode minus the conversion dropped, since ch06 now carries none while sibling files still do. (i) table captions follow the pending book convention, so do not touch them in isolation.

TIER 2, substantive rewrite or new content. (a) ch06:144-146: the Knight example's Strong value 5 must become 12 (Challenge-3 longsword triple 6/9/12), which moves the leather-armor outcome from 3 to 10 and the plate outcome from the asserted floor of 1 to 6; the narrative beat and Kael's HP consequence change, so this is a paragraph rewrite, not a typo. (b) the Fumble table (ch06:189-191): name the damage source for friendly fire, state whose roll the Off Balance Boon lands on given that NPCs never roll, and either publish an armor-degradation ladder or cut that entry. (c) ch06:65 versus ch06:181: add the sentence stating whether a fumbled attack still deals its Weak damage. (d) Worked Examples (ch06:234-242): add one opposed-roll example, one Boon/Bane example, and a sentence covering Critical and Fumble on a Defense Roll, since the social chapter sources the general rule to this chapter. (e) ch06:89: the Defense Roll trigger names only an NPC or monster attacker; add the hero-versus-hero and NPC-versus-NPC resolution line. (f) 13-combat:106-112: the Combat chapter points here for the full rule and then reproduces the same formulas, reversed outcome table, and defense examples; remove the duplicate and leave ch06 canonical. (g) ch06:43-47, 77-79, 122-124, 126-132: cut or fold two of the three rationale blocks and the back-to-back restatements, and refresh the Standard-tier copy that Table 6.1 shares with the introduction chapter.

TIER 3, design-flavored, canon or balance call. (a) ch06:160: decide how a core Critical scales; the locked convention forbids the doubling (a Master Strong of 21 becomes 42), and the canonical candidate is a single row up capped at 21, but that is a balance call because ch06 defines the general rule while ch09's tier bump is a talent. (b) ch06:101 plus glossary: rule on the three senses of 'Challenge' (per-roll penalty here, rating in ch13, monster difficulty in ch21), the sign flip between ch06's negative penalty and ch16's bare rating that is then subtracted, the goblin drift (ch06 -1, ch16 Challenge 1, bestiary 1/2), and its overlap with the Difficulty Modifier band; add a disambiguation line and a glossary entry. (c) armor degradation: ch16 models flat DR only, so decide ladder versus cut. (d) table-caption numbering, only 9 numbered in the book: set the convention before editing ch06.

ADJUDICATION. f-001 and f-002 do NOT conflict on the Knight. Both anchor the same line (06-core-resolution:144, with the plate branch at :146) and both expect the identical value, Strong 12, drawn from the Challenge-3 longsword triple at 20-bestiary:133 and corroborated by 13-combat:468's Standard-of-9. I reproduced the chain independently: the reversal table at ch06:114 sends a Weak Defense Roll to the NPC's Strong damage, canon fixes that at 12, so the printed 5 is wrong and the follow-ons are 10 (leather DR 2) and 6 (plate DR 6). It is a corroborating duplication, not a disagreement; implement once and credit both. f-003 and f-005 both establish book-wide convention faults; I reconcile them into one scope ruling. Both independently show the list regressions and the reference-format faults are migration artifacts, so the repair unit is the book, not the chapter. Their overlapping claims merge (doubled period, enum shape, bullet markers, caption partiality); the non-overlapping ones all survive (f-005's one-low chapter number; f-003's ch06-only minus drift). No contradiction between them.

SCOPE. Both list regressions are book-wide sweeps, not chapter-local fixes. Reason: the bare-line enum shape occurs in six chapter files (01:108, 02:26, 06:91, 19:339, 20:667, 22:239) and the hyphen-to-plus marker substitution runs 197 top-level lines across 11 files; a ch06-only patch leaves five enums and 192 bullet lines still broken and re-breaks ch06 on the next regeneration. ch06 is the highest-visibility symptom, not the scope. (The doubled period is likewise book-wide at 20 sites; the chapter number and minus drift are per-file.)

UNVERIFIED, for the orchestrator to re-check before implementing. (1) f-003's '9 of the book's 138 tables': I confirm 9 numbered captions, but the source shows 59 caption entries, so the 138 denominator is unreproduced. (2) f-003's pre-migration minus count of 7: the pre-migration reference yields 11, though the drift itself is real. (3) f-002's claim that a renamed ch04 Human gift heals the same 6: the Human gift in ch04 is a bonus Development Point, not a heal; a 6-HP heal does exist nearby (Second Breath, an Adept option), so the claim is misattributed even though the on-budget status of the 6 stands. (4) f-004's framing that ch06 renames Makeva with Lyra's class epithet overstates it: Makeva is herself an Odd, so the real defect is only the dropped surname. (5) f-002's mention of a 'Blinding Strike' value to audit: I confirm the term appears nowhere in the book, so its provenance as a defect source is unexplained. (6) f-001's identification of the bestiary 'Knight (Challenge 3)' as the Iron Circle adversary rests on the combat chapter's naming rather than the stat block itself.

payload.rationale: Topic t-01 drew seven refutes and zero supports across all seven voting members, and no refute was rebutted, so the topic closes as rejected under the charter's reject_quorum of 4 and check returns action=recommend without a judge. The members converged independently on the same load-bearing core: researcher (f-001) and game-architect (f-002) anchor the identical line for the Knight Strong-damage error and expect the identical value, and the librarian reproduced the chain independently against the reversal table and the Challenge-3 stat block, so the two are corroborating rather than conflicting. The layout-expert (f-003) and editor-in-chief (f-005) independently established that the list-rendering regressions and the doubled reference periods are migration artifacts whose repair unit is the book, not the chapter, and the librarian merged their overlapping claims into a single scope ruling. The contrarian (f-006) supplied the concrete counter-examples that make the Critical doubling and the undefined Fumble outcomes blocking rather than cosmetic, and the author (f-004) confirmed the chapter's voice and structure hold, which is why the disposition is a short substantive pass plus mechanical sweeps rather than a rewrite. The librarian enumerated six member claims it could not reproduce and the orchestrator re-verified them before implementing; nothing in the disposition rests on an unreproduced claim.
payload.recommendation: REJECT Chapter 6 (Core Resolution Mechanics) as a publishable unit, 7-0 (seven un-rebutted refutes, terminal reject-majority, no judge needed), and release it on one TIER 2 substantive rewrite pass plus TIER 1 mechanical micro-PRs. The hold is mechanical, not editorial: three load-bearing defects gate release (the Knight of the Iron Circle worked example prints a Strong value that contradicts the Challenge-3 stat block and both post-armor outcomes inherit it; the Critical table's top face doubles Strong damage onto no budget row and past the 21 ceiling; three Fumble entries are undefined and the fumble-as-automatic-failure line collides with the always-connect guarantee). Everything else is cosmetic and cheap. TIER 1 (mechanical, same-day micro-PR, zero mechanics change): restore the three Defense Roll formulas as three separate list items; restore the five defense definition lines as bullets; restore the intermediate arithmetic in the goblin defense line; correct the trailing greataxe clause that re-states the pre-DR figure; swap the lock example's skill to the roster's Thievery key; restore Makeva's surname; fix the armor cross-reference (doubled period and one-low chapter number); restore the Unicode minus glyphs. Do NOT touch table captions in isolation: caption numbering is a pending book-wide convention. TIER 2 (substantive rewrite or new content): correct the Knight example's Strong value to 12 and carry the consequences through both armor branches; complete the Fumble table (name the friendly-fire damage source, state where the Off Balance Boon lands given that NPCs never roll, and publish an armor-degradation ladder or cut that entry); state whether a fumbled attack still deals its Weak damage; add an opposed-roll example, a Boon/Bane example, and a Critical/Fumble-on-a-Defense-Roll sentence to the Worked Examples; add the hero-versus-hero and NPC-versus-NPC resolution line to the Defense Roll trigger; remove the duplicate Defense Roll formulas and outcome table from ch13 and leave ch06 canonical; cut or fold the redundant rationale blocks and restatements. TIER 3 (design-flavored, implement the recommended default and log as veto-able): replace Critical damage doubling with a single row up capped at the 21 ceiling; disambiguate the three senses of Challenge and add the glossary entry; resolve armor degradation as a cut (ch16 models flat DR only); set the table-caption convention book-wide before editing ch06. SCOPE RULING: both list-rendering regressions are BOOK-WIDE sweeps, not chapter-local fixes (the bare-line enum shape occurs in six chapter files; the hyphen-to-plus marker substitution runs 197 top-level lines across eleven files; a ch06-only patch leaves the rest broken and re-breaks on regeneration).

resolved.outcome: rejected 7-0 (seven un-rebutted refutes, zero supports, terminal reject-majority under reject_quorum 4; no judge, no impasse). Chapter 6 is held as not publishable as a unit and is released on one TIER 2 substantive pass plus TIER 1 mechanical micro-PRs, with the three TIER 3 design items implemented as recommended defaults and logged as veto-able.
